rows.citation: Gomes de Oliveira Neto, F., Dobslaw, F., Feldt, R. (2020). Using mutation testing to measure behavioural test diversity. 2020 IEEE International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation Workshops (ICSTW), pp. 254-263.
rows.model_type: general software (six small/medium open-source Maven Java projects with JUnit tests)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - PIT with all available mutation operators generates mutants; a test-by-mutant kill outcome matrix is built per project.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - many test cases act as diverse inputs, but these are existing unit tests, not designed stimulus protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - pass/fail test outcomes on Java code; no continuous traces or feature extraction.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - prioritises/selects test subsets under budgets by mutant-kill-pattern diversity; random and greedy-best comparators; not protocol design.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - killed mutants split 80/20 for diversity estimation versus APFD evaluation; no held-out projects or held-out operator family.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI or LLM-generated code changes studied.
rows.software: Uses the PIT mutation testing tool (URL not recorded); Docker-based replication package mentioned in paper (URL unverified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest conceptual analogue: mutant-kill matrix drives subset selection versus random. NeuroSem differs by continuous calibrated feature tolerances, neuron-model mutants, stimulus-protocol selection, and held-out models plus held-out mutation family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, authors, pages 254-263, Oct 2020); Semantic Scholar Graph API (abstract, arXiv id 2010.09144); arXiv abs page via WebFetch; full-text PDF arxiv.org/pdf/2010.09144 text-extracted with pypdf (PIT, six projects, 80/20 split, random and greedy-best comparators).

rows.citation: Zheng, W., Wu, X., Yang, X., et al. (2017). Test Suite Minimization with Mutation Testing-Based Many-Objective Evolutionary Optimization. 2017 International Conference on Software Analysis, Testing and Evolution (SATE), pp. 30-36.
rows.model_type: general software (three SIR repository programs plus the larger 'space' program)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - mutation score of candidate test suites is a primary optimization objective.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - selects among many existing test cases (inputs); not designed stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - code coverage and mutation score on benchmark programs; no signal features.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - six many-objective evolutionary algorithms (e.g. NSGA-II, MOEA/D-PBI) minimize suites trading cost, coverage and mutation score.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - abstract reports per-program results; no held-out program or held-out mutant family described; full text closed access.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Generic mutation-guided suite minimization, for which NeuroSem must not claim novelty. NeuroSem instead selects electrophysiology protocols for neuron models, with calibrated feature tolerances, cost-matched random baselines and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, six authors, pages 30-36, Nov 2017); OpenAlex works API (abstract via inverted index); Semantic Scholar Graph API (DBLP id conf/sate/ZhengWYCLL17; abstract elided, closed access).
